correctness.rationale: The binary-effect reduction is valid because each branch's optimal Bob success is a supremum of linear functionals of Alice's effect, so the two-branch objective is convex on the qubit effect interval and has a maximizing projection. The dependence on the out-of-trine-plane component can be removed and radial convexity pushes the remaining Bloch vector to the unit circle; trine symmetry reduces the projective axis to one sector. For each posterior weighted trine, the qubit Helstrom dual is exactly a smallest additively weighted enclosing-circle problem, with only pair-active and three-active possibilities. Substitution of the two branch posteriors gives the stated piecewise analytic score and shows the sector maximum occurs at the symmetry axis. At that point the active pair formula reduces to the displayed radical. Independently, a fresh 5001-point scan of the full symmetry sector using the pair/triple Helstrom-dual formulas attained 0.8975940487368783 only at the symmetry axis, agreeing with the closed value to machine precision; the scan is corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: This closes an explicitly visible certified numerical gap in a canonical nonlocal state-discrimination benchmark and quantifies exactly the operational cost of restricting Alice to one communicated bit. The result also identifies a simple optimal projective protocol and cleanly separates the \(m=2\) optimum from the known three-outcome one-way optimum, so it is a motivated exact communication-constrained invariant rather than an arbitrary finite optimization.
residual_risks: The exact calculation is special to trine symmetry and two Alice outcomes.

final_claim: For the equiprobable double-trine ensemble \(\{|s_i\rangle\otimes|s_i\rangle\}_{i=0}^2\), among one-round Alice-to-Bob LOCC protocols in which Alice has exactly two outcomes (one communicated bit) and Bob may use an arbitrary qubit POVM, the exact minimum-error success probability is \[\frac{4+\sqrt3+\sqrt{15+6\sqrt3}}{12}=0.897594048736878\ldots.\] An optimal protocol has Alice measure an in-plane Pauli observable aligned with a trine symmetry axis, after which Bob performs the optimal binary Helstrom measurement on the two active posterior states.
limitations: Exactly the double-trine ensemble, one Alice-to-Bob round, and a binary Alice message are covered.
Bob is unrestricted to arbitrary qubit POVMs; the result is not a statement about non-adaptive LOCC, two-way LOCC, or unrestricted one-way LOCC with more than two Alice outcomes.
The proof optimizes average minimum-error success, not unambiguous discrimination.
